title: Enforce a context-replay budget per fleet leaf

wiring.config_key: agent.contextBudget = { maxTokens: number, perFleet?: Record<string,number> } in harness.orchestrator.md (validated by validateWorkflowConfig)
wiring.fail_loud: Over-budget leaf emits an emitLog level:error effect naming the leaf + overage and is skipped (claimed, not dispatched) — never spends.
wiring.byte_identical_default: When agent.contextBudget is absent (or maxTokens<=0) the governor is a no-op; existing state-machine dispatch tests pass unchanged.

assumptions: REBASE onto main after sibling #1525 (budget governor) merged into the SAME handleTick dispatch loop: resolved so BOTH governors coexist and are ADDITIVE. state-machine.ts now consults the #1525 global spend envelope (isGlobalEnvelopeExhausted / isFleetAllocationExhausted) in the tick loop AND the #1524 per-leaf context budget (assertIssueWithinContextBudget) at the top of dispatchEligibleIssue — a leaf must pass BOTH gates. No #1525 logic removed; agent.budget (#1525) and agent.contextBudget (#1524) config fields both present; both governors' test suites green (28 #1525 budget-governor + 6 #1524 governor + 42 state-machine). PR remains MERGEABLE against main.

WIRING FOLLOW-UP (operator-directed): the core enforcement primitive now has a REAL live caller. The orchestrator dispatch governor consults assertIssueWithinContextBudget(config, issue) inside dispatchEligibleIssue BEFORE claiming/dispatching each leaf; an over-budget estimate throws ContextBudgetExceededError, which the state machine catches → emits a loud emitLog error effect + skips dispatch (no spend). Previously the primitive was barrel-exported but had zero live callers (set-but-never-read); that gap is now closed.

The per-leaf estimate at dispatch is a deterministic, I/O-free floor: (title + description).length / 4 tokens. spec/plans are file PATHS (not content) so they are not read in the pure state machine; a richer estimate (reading spec/plan files or reusing an enriched-spec token count) is a follow-up.

Byte-identical default is preserved: with no agent.contextBudget configured the governor returns immediately, so all pre-existing orchestrator dispatch tests pass unchanged (42-test state-machine suite green). Only an explicitly-configured budget changes behavior.

Landed the SMALLEST coherent slice: the per-leaf context-budget enforcement primitive (declared budget with a sane default DEFAULT_LEAF_CONTEXT_BUDGET_TOKENS=200000 + config override) enforced fail-loud at dispatch, now with a live orchestrator caller. Kept 'Refs #1524' (not 'Closes') because the issue's batching and outline/unfold-routing deliverables are deferred to follow-up slices.

Deferred to follow-up slices under #1524: (1) batching queue items per leaf to amortise the load; (2) routing leaf context through code_outline/code_unfold/find_context_for by default; (3) wiring the measured post-hoc cache-read into the lane provenance (the LeafContextSpend.cacheReadTokens field is defined but filled only once wired — the burn package already attributes cache-read per-lane via agentId); (4) the A/B-on-a-fixture-fleet acceptance criterion, which is a property of the batching/routing slices, not the enforcement primitive.
The budget ceiling is on the ASSEMBLED per-leaf context size (the number fan-out multiplies), not on cumulative replay (context_size x turns). Default 200000 tokens ~= a full large context window.

Primitives are pure/offline (no fs, no network, no token-counting library): the caller supplies the estimate, the primitive decides. This mirrors the fleet/claims module split (types own the shape, core owns the logic).

Kept the change localized to a NEW additive fleet/context-budget module to avoid colliding with sibling lanes #1525 (budget governor) and #1532 (rate-limit-aware fan-out), which touch adjacent shared dispatch/governor internals. No shared dispatch/governor file was refactored.

The canonical contract is stated once in docs/reference/fleet-family.md (new section 'The per-leaf context-replay budget'); individual member SKILL.md files reference it rather than restate it, so no per-fleet SKILL.md edit (and no 4-platform-mirror change) was needed for this slice.
